description: Figure 8 displays a line plot illustrating the average number of shared Top-6 routed experts across model layers for six different specialized tasks, as measured across two independent samples. The x-axis, labeled “Sample Token Count,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^9 to 2^20, with tick marks spaced at intervals of 2^10. The y-axis, labeled “Shared Experts for Two Samples,” ranges from 2.0 to 6.0. Six distinct lines represent the tasks: Intent (orange, square markers), Summary (blue, circle markers), Law (yellow, triangle markers), Translation (purple, diamond markers), Code (gray, cross markers), and Math (green, star markers). Each line shows the average shared expert count per layer as the sample token count increases. All lines begin near the bottom of the y-axis (around 2.0–3.0) at the smallest sample size (2^9) and generally trend upward, converging near the top of the y-axis (around 5.5–6.0) at the largest sample size (2^20). Notably, the Intent and Summary lines exhibit early increases followed by stabilization or slight declines, while the Law and Translation lines show more pronounced initial growth before leveling off. The Code line remains relatively low until around 2^16, after which it rises sharply. The Math line starts low and increases steadily throughout the range.
